question: Microsoft As Appropriate (AA) round with a senior head of an AI department (SDE-1 loop). The interviewer first asked how AI is used at the candidate's company (non-technical discussion), then asked the candidate to write working Tic-Tac-Toe code (a complete `playGame` method), then asked them to generate the same thing with ChatGPT and compare the output. A different Microsoft LLD round for Tic-Tac-Toe started from requirements and flow, drew a UML diagram, then coded `Player`, `PlayingPiece`, `PieceType` and `Board` for a 3 by 3 board with 2 players, later scaling it up.
lookingFor: Ability to turn a simple game into a clean object model.
Correct win and draw detection, ideally efficient.
Extensibility to N by N boards and more players.
Critical evaluation of AI-generated code rather than blind acceptance.
Communication of how AI is used responsibly at work.
followUps: How would you make win detection O(1) and extend it to N by N?
What would you change to support an AI opponent with minimax?
What mistakes did you find in the ChatGPT version, and how would you catch them?
How would you unit test this game?
What are the risks of using AI coding tools at work?
